mission: The SurveillanceDroneSwarm holds continuous watch over a tasked area of up to 25 km² and turns what happens there into acknowledged, triaged detection reports at the operations centre, inside the airspace clearance, weather, radio interference and satellite-positioning outages the environment imposes, using twelve battery-swapped drones, a mesh radio between them, a ground station and an intermittent link to the operations centre.
functionSentence: SurveillanceDroneSwarm moves the tasked area from unwatched and unreported to continuously watched and reported to the operations centre.

stakeholders.name: DutyController
stakeholders.role: Operations-centre operator who tasks the swarm, issues supervisory command and recall, and today does the sector assignment, handover, re-spread, deconfliction and relay by hand

stakeholders.name: OperationsCentreAnalyst
stakeholders.role: Judges the alerts the swarm raises, acknowledges each detection report and merges swarm tracks with the fixed camera network's tracks

stakeholders.name: AirspaceAuthority
stakeholders.role: Grants and withdraws the clearance that says when and where anything may fly; the swarm stays inside it and lands when it does not

stakeholders.name: GroundCrew
stakeholders.role: Services drones between sorties — swaps batteries at the recharge point in about 20 minutes — and recovers drones that return on their own

stakeholders.name: FixedCameraNetworkOperator
stakeholders.role: Keeps the existing fixed camera network and its own tracks, which stay in service and must be merged with what the swarm reports

stakeholders.name: ProgrammeAcquirer
stakeholders.role: Fields the twelve drones, chooses between the ground-centred and member-centred command-and-control architectures, and owns the placeholder numbers until the customer states them

environment.name: SurveillanceTasking
environment.doc: The area of interest, its sectors and the mission window, given by the operations centre.

environment.name: SupervisoryCommand
environment.doc: Priorities, a sector to look at more closely, and the reporting threshold — the least confidence a classification needs before it becomes a report.

environment.name: RecallOrder
environment.doc: An order to recall and land the whole swarm or one drone, issuable at any time.

environment.name: ReportAcknowledgement
environment.doc: The operations centre's confirmation of each detection report, so nothing is lost in a link gap.

environment.name: MovingObjectsInArea
environment.doc: The objects moving through the tasked area that the swarm must detect, classify and place in time and space.

environment.name: DetectionReports
environment.doc: Reports of detected objects with position, time, class or Unknown, confidence and provenance, delivered to the operations centre.

environment.name: TriagedAlerts
environment.doc: Reports ranked so that what is most likely to matter reaches the operator first, with duplicates merged.

environment.name: SwarmTrackPicture
environment.doc: One track per object — correlated across drones and handed over between sectors — to be merged with the fixed camera network's tracks at the operations centre.

environment.name: SwarmStatusPicture
environment.doc: Where every drone is, what it is doing, how much of the area is under watch and what is degraded.

environment.name: DecisionRecords
environment.doc: For every report: the frames it came from, the classifier version, the reporting threshold in force and who acknowledged it.

environment.name: AirspaceClearance
environment.doc: The airspace authority's clearance bounds when and where anything may fly; outside it a drone does not watch until it has landed.

environment.name: RadioInterference
environment.doc: A source of interference may degrade the mesh between drones as well as the link to the operations centre.

environment.name: SatellitePositioningOutage
environment.doc: Satellite positioning may be unavailable for minutes at a time; a drone then navigates by what its camera sees against stored maps.

environment.name: WeatherLightingAndDeception
environment.doc: Lighting, weather and deliberately misleading paint or shapes degrade what the sensors can tell apart; above moderate wind the swarm lands.

environment.name: FixedCameraNetwork
environment.doc: The existing camera network stays and keeps its own tracks; what the swarm reports must be mergeable with those tracks, not merely shown beside them.

environment.name: OperatorAttentionLimit
environment.doc: One operator supervises the whole swarm and can judge only a bounded number of alerts per hour, each needing time to judge.

environment.name: WatchAndReportOnlyScope
environment.doc: Weapons, interception and anything done to what is detected are out of scope: this system watches and reports.

environment.name: MeshRadioBetweenDrones
environment.doc: A radio mesh that carries coordination traffic between drones and does not depend on the link to the operations centre.

environment.name: GroundLinkToOperationsCentre
environment.doc: An intermittently available radio link carrying tasking, command, reports, status and acknowledgements.

environment.name: GroundStation
environment.doc: The station that tasks and watches the swarm and, in one of the two architectures, coordinates it.

environment.name: TwelveDroneFleet
environment.doc: Twelve identical small drones, each flying about 40 minutes, cruising at about 18 m/s and keeping about 3.0 km² under watch.

environment.name: BatterySwapAtRechargePoint
environment.doc: Ground crew and a recharge point where batteries are swapped, not charged in place — about 20 minutes of turnaround.

environment.name: RecoveryPoint
environment.doc: A point a drone that has lost contact with the swarm returns to on its own rather than becoming a hazard.

capabilities.name: ContinuousSectorWatch
capabilities.doc: Hold continuous surveillance of the tasked area: at any moment at least one drone is watching each sector of it, as members leave to recharge and rejoin.

capabilities.name: MovingObjectDetectionAndClassification
capabilities.doc: Detect moving objects in the area, classify them well enough to say whether they matter, and say Unknown rather than forcing a class when confidence is short of the reporting threshold.

capabilities.name: ReportDeliveryAndReconciliation
capabilities.doc: Deliver each detection report to the operations centre with position and time, keep detecting and holding reports while cut off, and reconcile once the link is back with none lost.

capabilities.name: SwarmSelfCoordination
capabilities.doc: Settle sector handover, recharge rotation, coverage redistribution, deconfliction, link relay, track correlation, track handover and member admission between the drones themselves over the mesh.

capabilities.name: OperatorSupervisionOfTheSwarm
capabilities.doc: Let one operator task, command, recall and watch the whole swarm rather than fly each drone, and acknowledge each report.

capabilities.name: AlertTriage
capabilities.doc: Triage reports before they reach the operator: what is most likely to matter first, duplicates merged, so the alert rate stays inside what one operator can judge.

capabilities.name: DecisionRecordKeeping
capabilities.doc: Keep, for every report, the frames it came from, the classifier version, the reporting threshold in force and who acknowledged it.

capabilities.name: GracefulDegradationUnderLoss
capabilities.doc: Keep flying and watching when a drone is lost, when the mesh is jammed and when the ground link or the ground station drops, with the loss of coverage bounded.

capabilities.name: AirspaceComplianceAndSafeRecovery
capabilities.doc: Stay inside the cleared airspace, land safely when it is not cleared or the weather exceeds moderate wind, and return to a recovery point when contact with the swarm is lost.

capabilities.name: ClassifierVersionConsistency
capabilities.doc: Keep one classifier version across the fleet and know which version each drone runs, so the same object is not classified differently by different drones.

moes.name: areaUnderWatchFraction
moes.doc: The share of the tasked area under watch at any moment; the brief states at least 0.9, and it separates architectures by how well they keep sectors filled while members rotate to recharge.

moes.name: coverageLossAfterMemberLossFraction
moes.doc: The share of coverage lost when one drone is lost, before the swarm re-spreads; the brief states no more than 0.25, and it is where a ground-coordinated and a member-coordinated redistribution differ most.

moes.name: coverageUnderMeshJammingFraction
moes.doc: The share of the area still under watch with half the links between drones jammed; the brief marks 0.75 as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, so meeting it means only that a placeholder has been met.

moes.name: reportAgeAtOperationsCentreSeconds
moes.doc: How old a report is when it reaches the operations centre with the link up; the brief marks 60 s as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and relay hop count drives it.

moes.name: positionErrorWithoutSatelliteMetres
moes.doc: A drone's position error after ten minutes without satellite positioning; the brief marks 50 m as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it decides whether reports place objects where they are.

moes.name: reportHoldWhileCutOffMinutes
moes.doc: How long a drone holds its reports while cut off without losing any; the brief marks 30 minutes as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it sizes on-board storage against the link-gap risk.

moes.name: missedDetectionFraction
moes.doc: The share of real objects that go undetected; the brief marks 0.10 as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it trades against the reporting threshold and the false-alarm rate.

moes.name: falseAlarmsPerHour
moes.doc: False alarms reaching the operator each hour; the brief marks 2 per hour as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it is the other side of the missed-detection trade.

moes.name: alertsReachingOperatorPerHour
moes.doc: How many alerts reach the operator each hour after triage; the brief marks 20 per hour as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it is what triage is scored on against operator overload.

moes.name: acknowledgedReportsThatMatterFraction
moes.doc: The share of reports the operator acknowledges that turn out to matter; the brief marks 0.8 as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it measures whether triage ranks the right things first.

moes.name: onboardClassificationCostUsdPerMember
moes.doc: What the on-board computing for classification costs per drone; the brief marks 300 USD as a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it decides how much classification can sit on the member rather than the ground.

moes.name: unattendedWatchDurationHours
moes.doc: How long the swarm holds the watch before it needs people — the brief asks for this but states no number, so 12 hours is a target set here and not asked for by the customer; it should be replaced by the customer's figure before any architecture is failed on it.

moes.name: fleetSizeMembers
moes.doc: Twelve drones is the fleet the design has to work with; the brief fixes it, so it is declared and never scored.

moes.name: memberEnduranceMinutes
moes.doc: Each drone flies about 40 minutes, and the transit out and back is spent from the same 40 minutes as the watching; the brief fixes it together with the 18 m/s cruise speed declared below, so the reach of a sector from the recharge point can be checked rather than assumed.

moes.name: groundTurnaroundMinutes
moes.doc: About 20 minutes on the ground because batteries are swapped, not charged in place; the brief fixes it and the airborne share follows from it with the endurance.

moes.name: cruiseSpeedMetresPerSecond
moes.doc: A drone cruises at about 18 m/s between its recharge point and its sector; the brief fixes it, and without it nothing can say whether a member reaches its station and returns inside the 40-minute endurance.

moes.name: instantaneousFootprintSquareKilometres
moes.doc: About 3.0 km² under watch at once from watch altitude; the brief fixes it, and it makes the coverage figure arithmetic from the number of drones airborne.

moes.name: areaOfInterestSquareKilometres
moes.doc: The area of interest is up to 25 km², divided into sectors; the brief fixes it as the size the design must cover.

moes.name: operatorSecondsPerAlert
moes.doc: The operator needs at least 30 seconds for each alert; the brief fixes this as the time an operator has, marked a placeholder awaiting the customer's number, and it is declared, never scored.

moes.name: trackStaleAfterSeconds
moes.doc: A track is marked stale once nothing has been seen for 120 seconds; the brief fixes this threshold and marks it a placeholder awaiting the customer's number.

moes.name: satellitePositioningOutageMinutes
moes.doc: The ten minutes without satellite positioning the position-error measure is taken over; it comes from the same placeholder statement as the 50 m figure and is a test condition, not a thing to be better at.

moes.name: meshLinksJammedFraction
moes.doc: The half of the links between drones jammed that the jammed-coverage measure is taken under; it comes from the same placeholder statement as the 0.75 figure and is a test condition.

population.doc: The swarm is twelve identical drones that must settle sector handover, recharge rotation, coverage redistribution, deconfliction, link relay, track correlation, track handover and member admission with each other over a mesh radio that does not depend on the link to the operations centre — that is what lets the watch survive when the ground link drops.

coordinationFunctions.name: handOverSector
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone leaving to recharge hands its sector to one arriving, without a gap in coverage.

coordinationFunctions.name: rotateRecharge
coordinationFunctions.doc: The drones settle who goes to recharge next, so that the airborne share never falls below what the sectors need.

coordinationFunctions.name: redistributeCoverage
coordinationFunctions.doc: When a drone is lost, the remaining ones re-spread over the sectors and the loss of coverage is bounded.

coordinationFunctions.name: deconflictFlight
coordinationFunctions.doc: The drones keep apart from each other in the air and at the recharge point.

coordinationFunctions.name: relayReportsThroughNeighbour
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone out of range of the ground station passes its reports and status through a neighbour.

coordinationFunctions.name: correlateTracks
coordinationFunctions.doc: When two drones see the same object, the swarm reports one track, not two.

coordinationFunctions.name: handOverTrack
coordinationFunctions.doc: When an object moves from one sector to the next, the drone watching the next sector takes over the track without losing it.

coordinationFunctions.name: admitMember
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone joins the coordination only after the others have authenticated it; one that fails is quarantined and takes no part until it has been readmitted.

c2Functions.name: taskSurveillanceArea
c2Functions.doc: The operator gives the area, its sectors and the mission window.

c2Functions.name: commandSupervisoryPriorities
c2Functions.doc: The operator sets priorities, names a sector to look at more closely, and sets the reporting threshold — the least confidence a classification needs before it becomes a report.

c2Functions.name: recallAndLand
c2Functions.doc: The operator recalls the whole swarm or one drone, at any time, and it lands.

c2Functions.name: presentStatusPicture
c2Functions.doc: The system shows where every drone is, what it is doing, how much coverage there is and what is degraded.

c2Functions.name: acknowledgeDetectionReport
c2Functions.doc: The operations centre confirms each detection report, so nothing is lost in a link gap.

hazards.name: PositionDriftHazard
hazards.doc: Without satellite positioning, a drone's position estimate drifts and its reports place objects in the wrong place.

hazards.name: MeshJammingHazard
hazards.doc: Interference cuts the links between drones, and coordination stalls.

hazards.name: MisclassificationHazard
hazards.doc: A detection is reported as the wrong class, or a forced class where Unknown was the truth.

hazards.name: SensingDegradedUnnoticedHazard
hazards.doc: A sensor degrades and nobody knows the reports from it are unreliable.

hazards.name: StaleTrackHazard
hazards.doc: A track is shown as current after nothing has seen the object for a while.

hazards.name: SpoofedMemberHazard
hazards.doc: Something that is not one of the drones joins the mesh and takes part in coordination.

hazards.name: MixedClassifierVersionsHazard
hazards.doc: Drones run different classifier versions and classify the same object differently.

hazards.name: OperatorOverloadHazard
hazards.doc: More alerts reach the operator than they can judge, and they accept what is in front of them.

rules.name: RecallWins
rules.doc: Once a drone is recalled, it does not watch again until it has landed.

rules.name: ReturnsWhenIsolated
rules.doc: From any situation a drone can be in, it can always get back to landed; an isolated drone included.

rules.name: GeofenceBreachEndsWatch
rules.doc: Once a drone is outside its cleared airspace, it does not watch until it has landed.

rules.name: QuarantinedStaysOut
rules.doc: Once a drone is quarantined, it takes no part in coordination until it has been readmitted.

modes.name: NavigationDegraded
modes.doc: The drone has no satellite positioning and navigates by what its camera sees against stored maps.

modes.name: SensingDegraded
modes.doc: The drone's sensors cannot be trusted as they are, and what it reports from them is marked accordingly.

modes.name: Isolated
modes.doc: The drone is cut off from the other drones and coordinates with none of them.

modes.name: Quarantined
modes.doc: The drone has failed admission and takes no part in coordination until it has been readmitted.

modes.name: MeshDegraded
modes.doc: A share of the links between drones is jammed and the swarm coordinates over what is left.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where the detected object was, as the reporting drone knew its own position at the time.

fields.name: objectClass
fields.doc: One of the known classes, or Unknown when the classification did not reach the reporting threshold.

fields.name: confidence
fields.doc: How sure the classification is, compared against the reporting threshold in force.

fields.name: sensorId
fields.doc: Which sensor the detection came from, so a degraded sensor's reports can be found.

fields.name: classifierVersion
fields.doc: The classifier version that produced the class, so mixed versions across the fleet are visible.

fields.name: ageSeconds
fields.doc: How long ago the detection was made, at the moment the report is read.

fields.name: trackId
fields.doc: The one identity the swarm reports for an object, held across correlation between drones and handover between sectors.

fields.name: lastSeenTime
fields.doc: When anything last saw the object on this track.

fields.name: stale
fields.doc: Set once nothing has been seen for the stale threshold — 120 seconds, a placeholder awaiting the customer's number.

rationale:
The environment reads cleanly into the four quadrants: tasking, supervisory command, recall and acknowledgement come in from the operations centre along with the objects moving through the area; reports, triaged alerts, one track per object, the status picture and the decision record go out; airspace clearance, interference, satellite outage, weather and deception, the fixed camera network that stays, and one operator's attention constrain it; twelve drones, the mesh, the intermittent ground link, the ground station and the 20-minute battery swap supply it. The mission sentence is those four read together, and the function sentence names the state change the whole model exists to make: a tasked area goes from unwatched and unreported to continuously watched and reported.

The system is a population, so the operational entity it takes over is one representative watch asset — the thing the duty controller assigns a sector to, hands a sector over from, re-spreads, deconflicts and relays through today. That is deliberate: those five hand-done activities become the coordination functions the members settle between themselves, and the controller's tasking, command, recall, status picture and acknowledgement become the C2 functions. Splitting them this way is what lets the two candidate architectures — coordination at the ground station, coordination on the drones — be compared on the same functions rather than on different ones.

The measures are the brief's numbers and nothing else. Every figure the brief marks a placeholder is carried as a placeholder so no report can claim the customer asked for it, and every figure the brief FIXES rather than asks the design to achieve — the fleet of twelve, the 40-minute endurance, the 20-minute turnaround, the 18 m/s cruise, the 3.0 km² footprint, the 25 km² area, the operator's 30 seconds, the 120-second stale threshold, and the two test conditions — is a budget: declared, constrained, never scored. The cruise speed matters most of these: with a 25 km² area and 40 minutes of flight, an architecture that puts its recharge point wrong can spend the whole budget on transit, and only a declared speed makes that visible. Only one target is invented — how long the watch holds before it needs people — and its doc says so, because a target nobody asked for can fail every architecture.

Common declares the flows, ports and interfaces in one place so the layers wire rather than invent: one MeshPort in the shape given, carrying a CoordinationMessage that every coordination item specialises, so one peer connection serves handover, rotation, redistribution, deconfliction, relay, correlation, track handover and admission; a member-to-ground port and an operations-centre port that keep the intermittent link and the operator boundary distinct, because one candidate architecture loads the first far more than the other; and clearance, scene and servicing ports so the constraining and supplying environment has somewhere to attach at OA and SA. DetectionReport and Track carry exactly the fields the brief lists, which is why the acknowledgement key sits beside a report rather than inside it.
